structured_output.analysis: The best grid iso_3.15 uses 3.14795 bits per weight against a budget of 3.1484375, so almost no budget is left. For every top-loss layer, the method it already has is the lowest-KL choice at its bit width. Examples: 3.up_proj rht_gptq_int3 0.00642 vs gptq_int3 0.00706; 27.up_proj gptq_int3 0.00572 vs rht_gptq_int3 0.00774. Upgrading a layer costs about 1 bit per weight on a 3.1M-parameter layer. To pay for that I would need a cheap downgrade, but the retrieved records give no low-loss downgrade candidate. Moving any of the listed layers from int3 to int2 costs roughly 0.02 KL. Changing per-layer methods therefore has no measured gain left. I am using this round to test GPTQ options that cost no bits: act_order and damp. The quip_e8p record E111111111111 is for a method that is not in the option space, so I ignored it.

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder
proposals.rationale: Uses the same per-layer methods as iso_3.15 (KL 0.436, E514ab09c524e), so the bit count is unchanged. The only change is act_order=true for all GPTQ variants. The worst layers are GPTQ layers, for example 27.up_proj gptq_int3 at 0.00572 (Ef04d8aa7bded) and 14.down_proj rht_gptq_int2 at 0.00633 (E4c3f9b73e065).

proposals.name: iso_3.15_actorder_damp05
proposals.rationale: Uses the same methods and bit count as iso_3.15 (KL 0.436, E514ab09c524e), with act_order=true and damp=0.05. The goal is more stable GPTQ updates on layers with heavy-tailed activations, such as 27.up_proj (activation kurtosis 1090.09, E24beed188b6a; gptq_int3 KL 0.00572, Ef04d8aa7bded).
